Eighth development release of 0.19.0: PDF reports for devices, prefixes and IP addresses, OSPF, IS-IS and static routes on the Routing tab with a VRF picker and checks, and bulk select on every remaining list page.

> [!CAUTION]
> **This is a development release. It is not stable and it contains bugs.** Do not run it in production or on data you can't restore. Take a backup before upgrading a test install, and expect behaviour to change before 0.19.0. If you run into a problem, please [submit a bug report](https://github.com/danbyte-net/danbyte/issues/new?template=bug_report.md) - every report helps get 0.19.0 right.

> [!NOTE]
> **Behaviour changes:**
> - **Users, groups and permissions guard against lock-out everywhere.** Deactivating or deleting your own account, the last active superuser, a built-in group, the built-in Administrator grant, or the last group or grant through which you manage users is refused - on a single page and in bulk alike.
> - **Script export and import see only the scripts you can see.** Export used to include other people's private scripts.
> - **DHCP scopes and DNS zones are export-only** in import/export; an import could never create them.

### Reports

- **PDF reports** of devices, prefixes and IP addresses: **PDF report…** on their pages, in the lists' Import / Export menu (the rows shown) and in the bulk bar (the rows selected). Pick the title, paper and orientation, the list columns (custom fields included) in your own order, grouping, a summary by status, role and site, and one page per object with the sections you want - interfaces, addresses, cables, software with licences, ports, lifecycle, monitoring, utilisation, child prefixes, ranges, NAT, DNS, journal and change log, each with its own columns. Tables carry status, role and tag badges in their colours. API: `/api/devices/report/`, `/api/prefixes/report/`, `/api/ips/report/`.

### Topology

- **OSPF and IS-IS on the Routing tab.** Adjacencies found through cables (and patch panels), or a shared subnet where not cabled, drawn dashed (OSPF, with area and costs) and dotted (IS-IS, with level and metric); their panels show both interfaces, timers, MTU, BFD and the keychain name.
- **Static routes** as arrows to their next-hop router, labelled with the route count.
- **VRF picker:** all tables (the default, as before), the global table or one VRF.
- **Checks:** a chip that lists, and rings on the map, BGP sessions defined on one side only, AS mismatches, and OSPF area, timer and MTU or IS-IS level mismatches across a cable.

### Lists

- **Bulk select on every remaining list:** certificates, certificate requests and issuers, DHCP scopes, reservations and leases, DNS zones, L2VPNs, virtual switches, virtualization sources, Windows servers, automation targets, config contexts and bundles, export and label templates, webhooks, scripts, maintenance, dashboards, jobs, Oxidized nodes, users, groups and permissions. Export, bulk edit and safe bulk delete where a single page allows them; Enable / Disable, Activate / Deactivate, Requeue and Cancel where those exist. Secrets, keys and passwords are never exported. DHCP scopes and reservations are deleted on the Windows server one by one; a refusal keeps that row with the server's reason.
